cohort: The study included 4649 women in Ghana who had given birth within the past five years.
finding: The prevalence of caesarean section delivery in Ghana was 20.1%, with age, educational level, wealth index, religion, parity, twin status, access to healthcare, self-reported health status, and region identified as significant determinants.
mod_finding: Age, educational level, wealth index, religion, parity, twin status, access to healthcare, self-reported health status, and region significantly determined the likelihood of caesarean section delivery.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from women regarding births that occurred within the past five years prior to the study.
